title: Option strategies I: directional and income
objectives: Build covered call and protective put.
body_md:
## Protective put

Own shares **and buy a put**. Loss is capped at (purchase price − strike + premium). Like insurance.

## Covered call

Own shares **and sell a call**. Earns premium, caps the upside above the strike. Suits a neutral to mildly bullish view.

## Bull call spread

Buy a lower-strike call, **sell a higher-strike call**. Cheaper than a lone call, with capped gain.

Example: buy 100 call at 8, sell 110 call at 3. **Net debit 5; max profit 5 (spot ≥ 110); max loss 5; breakeven 105.**

## Bear put spread

Buy a higher-strike put, sell a lower-strike put. Profits from a fall, with limited risk.

## Comparison

| Strategy | View | Risk | Reward |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protective put | Bullish with protection | Limited | Unlimited |
| Covered call | Neutral to mild bull | Stock falls | Premium plus limited gain |
| Bull call spread | Moderately bullish | Net debit | Limited |

> **Exam tip:** Spreads cut cost and cap both gain and loss.
example: A holder of a stock at 500 buys a 480 put for 10. Worst case: sell at 480; total loss = 20 + 10 = 30 per share.
say: A spread lowers the cost but also caps the gain.
A covered call gives income but gives up big rallies.
never: A covered call has unlimited upside.

check.q: Bull call spread: buy 100 call @8, sell 110 call @3. Maximum loss is:

o: Own stock and buy a put
Sell stock and sell a put
Has unlimited loss on the option
check.why: The sold call caps the gain above the strike.
